# NarrativeTrace

> Code is the log. Auto-generate human-readable execution traces from method names, parameter names, and return values.

NarrativeTrace is a TypeScript library that eliminates manual logging. It wraps objects with ES Proxy to capture every method call and renders the result as Markdown, prose, diagrams, or JSON. It propagates trace identity across fork/join, fire-and-forget and asynchronous-snapshot boundaries — and the work traced across those boundaries comes back into the launching trace — bridges to OpenTelemetry/Winston/Pino, and includes naming clarity analysis that scores code readability and gates builds.

## Start here (paste this into your agent)

```text
Set up NarrativeTrace in this project and show me its first trace.
1. Read https://narrativetrace.ai/typescript/llms.txt first. It carries the install block and the
known traps. Do not guess versions or artifact names.
2. If this directory has no project yet, create the smallest console app that
llms.txt's "Install and first trace" block describes. Otherwise work inside the existing
project and trace one real service boundary.
3. Add `@narrativetrace/cli` as a dev dependency the way llms.txt shows, then run
`npx @narrativetrace/cli init --dry-run` and show me the diff. It installs the
NarrativeTrace agent skills into this project and adds a marked section to AGENTS.md. Run
it for real only after I have seen the diff.
4. If the `add-narrative-tracing` skill is now available, follow it. Otherwise follow the
"Install and first trace (copy this)" block in llms.txt.
5. Add one test that traces a call with a deny-listed parameter and asserts the trace
shows `[REDACTED]` for it.
6. Run the program, then run the doctor (`npx @narrativetrace/cli doctor`). Paste
the trace and the doctor report, explain the trace in two sentences, and list exactly what
changed in the project.
Rules: never disable redaction; do not commit `.received.nt` files; pass
parameter names to `traceObject` explicitly so arguments never render as `arg0`; run
everything in the foreground and read the output before you report; if you cannot fetch
URLs, say so and I will paste llms.txt.
```

## Install and first trace (copy this)
Node 20+ required. In an empty directory `npm init -y` comes first — without a `package.json` the next line fails with `ENOENT`. `npm pkg set type=module` must come before `npm add`, or step 2 throws `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`; with pnpm/yarn run their own `init` instead, which already defaults to it:
```bash
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm add @narrativetrace/core-node @narrativetrace/proxy
npm add -D @narrativetrace/vitest vitest
npm add -D @narrativetrace/cli
```
<!-- snippet: examples/sixty-seconds/index.js -->
```js
// index.js
import { NarrativeTraceConfig, SyncNarrativeContext, renderMarkdownBody } from "@narrativetrace/core-node";
import { traceObject } from "@narrativetrace/proxy";

class OrderService {
  placeOrder(customerId, productId, quantity) {
    return `ORD-${customerId}-${productId}-${quantity}`;
  }
}

// serviceName is what the platform and the OTel bridge show for this service; without it, traces
// read "unknown_service:node". Trace a class instance — a plain object would narrate as "Object".
const context = new SyncNarrativeContext(new NarrativeTraceConfig(), {
  serviceName: "order-service",
});
const service = traceObject(new OrderService(), context, {
  placeOrder: ["customerId", "productId", "quantity"],
});

service.placeOrder("C1", "P1", 2);
console.log(renderMarkdownBody(context.captureTrace()));
```
<!-- /snippet -->
The TypeScript runtime needs this configuration code and reads none of it from anywhere else: `serviceName` sets the service identity, a class instance (never an object literal, which narrates as `Object.<method>`) gives spans their class name, and the parameter names are passed explicitly. The platform and the OTel bridge show these strings to someone else; without them they read `unknown_service:node`, `Object.checkout` and `arg0`. The same identity can come from `NARRATIVETRACE_SERVICE_NAME`, `NARRATIVETRACE_SERVICE_VERSION` and `NARRATIVETRACE_ENVIRONMENT`: an `AsyncNarrativeContext` reads them itself, and a `SyncNarrativeContext` takes `{ ...serviceIdentityFromEnv() }` (from `@narrativetrace/core-node`).
Tracing attaches only to what you wrap (`traceObject`, or the providers the NestJS module discovers). `exclude` — an option, or `NARRATIVETRACE_EXCLUDE` — names class-name prefixes that are never traced; stating it replaces a shipped default of NestJS internals, and a built-in list (runtime hooks, a `class` member, a foreign `bind()` copy) is never wrapped whatever you state. Both lists are in the configuration guide.
Run `node index.js`. Expected output (your duration will differ):
<!-- snippet: examples/sixty-seconds/narrativetrace-output/sixty-seconds/console-output.txt mask=duration -->
```text
- `OrderService.placeOrder(customerId: "C1", productId: "P1", quantity: 2)` → `"ORD-C1-P1-2"` — 0.29ms #1
```
<!-- /snippet -->
Add `index.test.js` next to it — this is the prompt's own step 4, proving redaction:
<!-- snippet: examples/sixty-seconds/index.test.js -->
```js
// index.test.js
import { renderMarkdownBody } from "@narrativetrace/core-node";
import { traceObject } from "@narrativetrace/proxy";
import { createNarrativeTest } from "@narrativetrace/vitest";
import { expect } from "vitest";

const test = createNarrativeTest();

class PaymentService {
  charge(customerId, paymentToken) {
    return `CHG-${customerId}`;
  }
}

test("redacts a deny-listed parameter", ({ narrativeContext }) => {
  const service = traceObject(new PaymentService(), narrativeContext, {
    charge: ["customerId", "paymentToken"],
  });

  service.charge("C1", "tok_live_51H8x");

  expect(renderMarkdownBody(narrativeContext.captureTrace())).toContain("[REDACTED]");
});
```
<!-- /snippet -->
Run `npx vitest run`. It passes, and the rendered trace inside it shows `[REDACTED]` for `paymentToken`.

## Runtime support
Which package runs where, as far as this repository can show. "Tested" means a test in this repository asserts it; "expected to work" means the sources make no Node-only demand but nothing here runs it there.

| Package | Imports from Node | Node 20+ | Cloudflare Workers | Browser | Deno / Bun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@narrativetrace/core` | none (architecture test) | tested | expected to work | expected to work | expected to work |
| `@narrativetrace/proxy` | none (architecture test) | tested | expected to work | expected to work | expected to work |
| `@narrativetrace/core-node` | `node:async_hooks`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs` | tested | needs the `nodejs_compat` flag; not tested here | no | not tested here |
| `@narrativetrace/core-web`, `@narrativetrace/browser`, `@narrativetrace/standalone` | none (architecture test) | tested | expected to work | intended runtime | expected to work |

What `core-node` uses each built-in for: `node:async_hooks` is `AsyncLocalStorage`, the per-request scope behind `AsyncNarrativeContext`; `node:crypto` is the random source for trace and span ids; `node:fs` reads the optional project config file and is only called through `resolveConfig`, `readFileConfig` or `readProjectFile`. The imports sit at module load, so the runtime must provide all three modules even if you never read a file. `core` and `proxy` mint ids from Web Crypto (`globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues`) when no runtime adapter registered a generator. Where `AsyncLocalStorage` is unavailable, `SyncNarrativeContext` from `core` needs no Node module — but it does not isolate concurrent requests from each other.

## Tracing a request in production
One `AsyncNarrativeContext` per process, one `context.run(...)` per request, the export inside it. Import `AsyncNarrativeContext` from `@narrativetrace/core-node` — `core` does not export it publicly. `captureTrace()` MUST be called inside `run()`: it reads the current scope, so outside it you read the process-wide default scope, which holds none of the request's spans, and the tree comes back empty. Call `reset()` in a `finally`, so a throwing export cannot leave the request's spans in the shared pipeline.
<!-- snippet: examples/express/src/request-scope.ts -->
```ts
import {
  AsyncNarrativeContext,
  NarrativeTraceConfig,
  renderIndentedText,
} from "@narrativetrace/core-node";
import { traceObject } from "@narrativetrace/proxy";

// One context for the process; one run() scope per request.
export const context = new AsyncNarrativeContext(new NarrativeTraceConfig());

class OrderService {
  placeOrder(customerId: string, quantity: number): string {
    return `ORD-${customerId}-${quantity}`;
  }
}

const orders = traceObject(new OrderService(), context, { placeOrder: ["customerId", "quantity"] });

export async function handleRequest(
  customerId: string,
  exportTrace: (trace: string) => void = console.log,
): Promise<string> {
  return context.run(async () => {
    try {
      const orderId = orders.placeOrder(customerId, 2);
      // captureTrace() reads the current scope: call it here, inside run().
      exportTrace(renderIndentedText(context.captureTrace()));
      return orderId;
    } finally {
      context.reset();
    }
  });
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->
The console line is the simplest export. To send the same spans to a real sink, give the context a pipeline that carries a consumer next to the buffered one that backs `captureTrace()`: `@narrativetrace/pino` (`createPinoEventConsumer`), `@narrativetrace/winston` (`createWinstonEventConsumer`) or `@narrativetrace/opentelemetry` (`createOtelEventConsumer`) — the wiring is in the [Framework Integration Guide](framework-integration-guide.md), sections 8 and 9. `@narrativetrace/express` and `@narrativetrace/hono` ship middleware that opens the per-request `run()` for you.

To trace a module of plain functions rather than a class, wrap them as one object and re-export the traced copies — `const { fn: tracedFn } = traceObject({ fn }, context, { className: "Pricing", methods: { fn: { params: ["a", "b"] } } }); export { tracedFn as fn };` — see "Tracing a module of plain functions" in the Framework Integration Guide for the limit. A bundler that evaluates your entry and your handlers as separate module graphs (OpenNext, Next custom servers, Workers wrapper entries) needs one shared context: "Sharing one context across bundles" in the same guide.

## Before you start
- Install every `@narrativetrace/*` package at one version: each peers on `@narrativetrace/core` at the exact version it was published with (`core-node` and `core-web` depend on it the same way), so mixed versions end in `ERESOLVE`.
- Licence: free and source-available under BSL 1.1 (Apache 2.0 four years after each release); the terms are in each package's `LICENSE` and the `license` field is `BUSL-1.1`.
- Parameter names of classes you don't own are lost at compile time — pass them explicitly (`traceObject(target, context, { placeOrder: [...] })`) or every argument renders as `arg0`, `arg1`, ...; unrecognised option keys there throw, naming the accepted ones, rather than being silently ignored.
- `@narrativetrace/vitest` peers on vitest `1.x`, `2.x`, or `3.x` (tested, not just declared); register `ClaritySuiteReporter`/`GlossarySuiteReporter` from the `@narrativetrace/vitest/reporters` subpath in `vitest.config.ts`, never the package root — the root also loads `vitest` itself, which crashes config loading on every version.
- `DualPathPipeline`'s buffered argument defaults itself when `null`/omitted, so adding a Winston/Pino/OTel consumer never makes `captureTrace()` silently empty; pass an explicit `new BufferedEventConsumer()` when you want to size it yourself.
- Test trace output is on by default (`NARRATIVETRACE_OUTPUT=false` opts out).
- `createNarrativeTest` also writes a value-free `.nt` structural artifact per scenario (last-green baseline, "Since last green" console delta) with no configuration needed; `approval: true` turns on approval traces (`.approved.nt`/`.received.nt`, promote with `pnpm run approve-narratives`). Use `createNarrativeTest(...).each(cases)` — this port's own thin `.each`, not Vitest's native one — for a per-invocation `.nt`/approval identity.
- A Vitest run has a name — one three-word phrase (`runIdentity()`) named in the console footer (`run: bold elk soars`), `manifest.json`'s top-level `run` object, and every Markdown trace's `run:` frontmatter; pass `runIdentity().name` as `runName` to `createPinoEventConsumer`/`createWinstonEventConsumer`/`createEnricherEventConsumer` to carry it into your own logs too. Never reaches the structural `.nt` artifact, an approved/received trace, or the delta computation.

## Agent skills
- `add-narrative-tracing` — Installs NarrativeTrace into a TypeScript project and gets it to a first trace. Use when NarrativeTrace is not yet installed, a project needs its very first traced call, or traces need to reach a real logger instead of a bare console.log.
- `narrativetrace-doctor` — Diagnoses a NarrativeTrace TypeScript install and configuration. Use when nothing is being traced, traces aren't showing up, the vitest config crashes on load, parameter names render as arg0/arg1, or you are not sure NarrativeTrace is wired up correctly. Read-only — makes no changes.
- `narrativetrace-feedback` — Reports a defect in NarrativeTrace itself: a doctor check that is wrong or whose fix does not work, a skill step that cannot be followed, wording in the install prompt that led somewhere wrong, or the library misbehaving on a correctly configured project. Drafts the report from your project (the install coordinates, the doctor's own JSON report, and at most one structural trace), refuses to write one that carries a value from your traces and names the rule that refused it, shows you the whole draft, and asks once whether to file it publicly. Files nothing without your answer and sends nothing anywhere. Say 'report this to NarrativeTrace' or 'the doctor's fix did not work' to invoke it.
- `add-narrativetrace-clarity` — Adds or verifies NarrativeTrace Clarity in a TypeScript Vitest project. Use when you want a first naming report, per-element explanations, renames for unclear names, or an explicit clarity quality gate. Registers the clarity reporter in the Vitest config, runs the suite, checks the fresh nonempty results file, reads the scores and issues, applies the report's rename suggestions and re-runs until the gate is clean, and preserves existing thresholds. Route tracing itself being broken to narrativetrace-doctor.
- `narrativetrace-verify` — Verifies a change by reading what the code actually did before saying it is done. Use after the tests are green and before reporting a change that crosses collaborators, branches, retries, runs async, carries state between calls, or touches code not written in this session — and skip it, saying why, for a pure function or a one-class edit. Writes the intent down first, runs the smallest real path, reads the value-free structural trace against the intent, opens values only on the span that looks wrong, then pins the flow as an approval baseline behind your yes and reports what the trace showed, citing span ids (`#1.3`).
- `narrativetrace-debug` — Finds the cause of a wrong result by reading what the code did with the values, not by stepping through it. Reproduces the symptom with tracing on, names the first span where a value diverges by its span id before changing any code, fixes it there, checks the structural trace shows nothing else moved, pins the reproduction as a regression test and an approval baseline behind your yes, and reports the root cause by span id. Hands a defect in NarrativeTrace itself to narrativetrace-feedback.
- `narrativetrace-explain` — Explains what an application or a flow actually does, with nothing broken and no change needing verification. Decides first whether a trace is worth it (a question ten lines of source answer is answered from the source, with no install and no run), otherwise runs one existing scenario with tracing on, reads the value-free structural trace in the order it ran, and explains the run by span id, marking what it inferred and naming the code no span covered. Hands a defect to narrativetrace-debug, a change to narrativetrace-verify.

`npx --yes @narrativetrace/cli init` installs all seven under `.claude/skills/{narrativetrace-doctor,add-narrative-tracing,narrativetrace-feedback,add-narrativetrace-clarity,narrativetrace-verify,narrativetrace-debug,narrativetrace-explain}/` (the directory Claude Code loads, written on every project; `--vendor none` leaves it out), `.agents/skills/{narrativetrace-doctor,add-narrative-tracing,narrativetrace-feedback,add-narrativetrace-clarity,narrativetrace-verify,narrativetrace-debug,narrativetrace-explain}/` (Codex), and the always-on `AGENTS.md` pointer, in one step — `--dry-run` first to preview the diff. Copying the rendered files by hand still works too. Full descriptions and triggers: [Agent Skills](agent-skills.md). Per-platform install paths — Cursor, Replit, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code — and the pointer files `init` writes for them: [Use NarrativeTrace with your agent](use-with-your-agent.md).

They are also reachable from two registries, each landing the same pages `init` then adopts. The Claude Code plugin marketplace carries them too: `/plugin marketplace add narrativetrace/narrativetrace-typescript`, then `/plugin install narrativetrace-typescript@narrativetrace-typescript` — then run `npx --yes @narrativetrace/cli init --dry-run`, read the diff, and run it without the flag so `AGENTS.md` points at them. `npx skills add narrativetrace/narrativetrace-typescript` installs the open-standard pages directly into the project — then run `npx --yes @narrativetrace/cli init --dry-run`, read the diff, and run it without the flag so `AGENTS.md` points at them.

## The doctor
```bash
npx --yes @narrativetrace/cli doctor
```
The install block above does not put the CLI in your project — `npx` fetches it on demand, and `--yes` keeps that fetch from stopping at a confirmation prompt; add `@narrativetrace/cli` as a dev dependency if you want it resolved locally. Read-only, zero network: it reads `package.json`, resolvable packages, and your source/test files, and prints a one-liner, a fix and a doc link per finding. Twenty-eight checks: toolchain versions, config shape, the common traps (silent sink, `arg0` parameters, a traced plain object that narrates as `Object`, a service with no name set, an exclude list the runtime would reject, unproven redaction, stale approval traces, committed approval baselines with approval mode off, a project that never read llms.txt), whether the agent skills above are installed under `.agents/skills/` and stamped with the release this project resolves — and one per framework the project uses, from the framework table the installed doctor carries: the framework is detected but its integration is not installed, or installed but never wired, and the fix prints the install line and the wiring. Exit `0` clean, `1` findings, `2` could not run.

<!-- covered-frameworks:begin -->
Covered frameworks (each row of the doctor's framework table): Vitest (`config.vitest-fixture`); Express (`config.express-middleware`); Hono (`config.hono-middleware`); NestJS (`config.nestjs-module`); Angular (`config.angular-provider`); React (`config.react-provider`); React Router (`config.react-router-capture`); Pino (`config.pino-consumer`); Winston (`config.winston-consumer`); OpenTelemetry (`config.opentelemetry-consumer`); Default logger (Pino) (`trap.silent-sink`); Fastify (no integration shipped, `config.fastify-integration` reports it); Koa (no integration shipped, `config.koa-integration` reports it).
<!-- covered-frameworks:end -->

## Report a problem

If NarrativeTrace, this file, a skill or the doctor is wrong, ask your agent to use the `narrativetrace-feedback` skill: it drafts the report from your project, refuses to write one that carries a value from your traces, shows you the whole thing, and files nothing until you say so. Nothing is sent anywhere — the draft is yours until you submit it yourself.

<!-- snippet: packages/skills-catalogue/src/catalogue/feedback-commands.ts region=reportCommands -->
```ts
const REPORT_FLAGS =
  '--category <category> --step "<where it happened>" --did "<what you did>"' +
  ' --happened "<what happened>" --expected "<what you expected>"';

/** Drafts the report, checks it carries no values, and prints the whole thing. */
export const DRAFT_REPORT = `npx @narrativetrace/cli feedback draft ${REPORT_FLAGS}`;

/** Prints the pre-filled issue-form URL for the same report, once the user has said yes. */
export const PRINT_URL = `npx @narrativetrace/cli feedback url ${REPORT_FLAGS}`;
```
<!-- /snippet -->

`feedback draft` writes `narrativetrace-output/feedback/feedback-draft.md` and `feedback-body.md`, and exits 2 naming a `vf.*` rule if a field carries a value instead of a description. `feedback url` then prints the pre-filled issue form for `github.com/narrativetrace/narrativetrace-typescript`, which you open and submit under your own account, pasting the body file into its last box; `feedback gh` prints the exact `gh issue create` line when `gh` is signed in, and never runs it. Filing is public: it shows that your project uses NarrativeTrace.

## Recipes

One page per problem, in the words a user would type. Each page carries its scenario's code and the real output of a run this build performs — nothing on a recipe page is typed by hand.

- [Add logging to this service](recipes/add-logging-to-this-service.md) — a checkout with no log statement: wrap its collaborators once and every call, with its parameter names and its result, appears in the project's own pino logger.
- [Help me debug and fix this bug](recipes/help-me-debug-and-fix-this-bug.md) — a declined card leaves the stock reserved: the failing run's narrative shows `reserve`, then `charge` throwing, then nothing, and the fix and the approved baseline that pins it.
- [Why did this test fail](recipes/why-did-this-test-fail.md) — a red checkout test read span by span against the assertion, where every span agrees with every other and the expectation is what is stale.
- [Review a complex flow before changing it](recipes/review-a-complex-flow-before-changing-it.md) — one run at `detail` and at `summary`, with the log line that carries values beside the value-free `.nt` an agent reads.
- [Review a refactoring: did behaviour change](recipes/review-a-refactoring-did-behaviour-change.md) — the tests stay green, the approval diff names the dropped call, and `narrativetrace-approve` is how you say yes.
- [Follow one request across services (distributed tracing)](recipes/follow-one-request-across-services.md) — the checkout charges through a second traced service over a real socket: `tracedFetch` puts the W3C `traceparent` on the request, so one trace id is in both services' log lines and the header names the caller's `charge` span as the parent.
- [Keep secrets out of the logs](recipes/keep-secrets-out-of-the-logs.md) — a password caught by its parameter name and a card number caught by its value, in the log and in the narrative, with the test that reads the log back as the proof.
- [Follow a flow across threads](recipes/follow-a-flow-across-threads.md) — two tasks handed to a `ForkJoinGroup` keep the customer's trace id and come home under the span that launched them; the same job handed to a worker without the handover starts a trace nobody is searching for.
- [Send traces to the observability stack you already run](recipes/send-traces-to-the-observability-stack-you-already-run.md) — one run, two consumers: the narrative lines your logger already writes beside the OpenTelemetry spans the same events became, attribute by attribute, redactions included.
- [Trace in production without the cost](recipes/trace-in-production-without-the-cost.md) — one declined checkout at `detail` and at `errors`, where a run that succeeded writes no artifact at all, and only `off` skips interception.

## Field notes from AI agents (self-reported, not a benchmark)
We asked AI agents to build a claims service with NarrativeTrace and write up the experience for another engineer, naming what was awkward. Prompted, one run each, unedited, model named; we wrote the library. The reports so far are from the Java runtime; the same exercise runs for TypeScript next, and the principle they describe — the trace as evidence, redaction by parameter name, output on by default — is the same here. All six reports, the exact prompt and the task: https://narrativetrace.ai/#agents-saying
- "…the release call is present, generated from a real run, not asserted from inside the process being tested." — Claude Sonnet, 2026-09-11
- "The always-on name-based deny-list is a genuinely nice piece of design: naming a parameter `paymentToken` gets you redaction for free, and I could prove it in a test." — Claude Sonnet, 2026-09-11
- "The trace of a failed payment made missing compensation immediately visible, and approval testing caught an extra call that ordinary value assertions accepted." — GPT-6, 2026-09-08

## Docs

- [Complete Reference](llms-full.md): Full API reference, 18-package map, configuration, concurrency, integration guides, architecture decisions, and troubleshooting
- [Framework Integration Guide](framework-integration-guide.md): Express, Hono, browser, and AsyncLocalStorage integration paths, with the shared-context safety notes
  - Outbound `traceparent` on Node: `tracedFetch(ctx)` (global `fetch`) and `traceparentHeaders(ctx)` (any other HTTP client), both from `@narrativetrace/core-node`, send the current span's `traceparent` so an instrumented callee joins the caller's trace — the same call as the browser's `tracedFetch`.
- [Agent Skills](agent-skills.md): `add-narrative-tracing` — install and first trace, ending at the doctor — `narrativetrace-doctor` — a thin, read-only agent skill over `npx --yes @narrativetrace/cli doctor` — `narrativetrace-feedback` — report a defect in NarrativeTrace with your approval — and `add-narrativetrace-clarity` — a first naming report and an optional clarity gate over the Vitest reporter, installable today via `.claude/skills/{add-narrative-tracing,narrativetrace-doctor,narrativetrace-feedback,add-narrativetrace-clarity}/`, `.agents/skills/{add-narrative-tracing,narrativetrace-doctor,narrativetrace-feedback,add-narrativetrace-clarity}/` (Codex), or the always-on `AGENTS.md` pointer

## Sections in Complete Reference

- Overview and philosophy
- Quick start (install and trace)
- Package map with dependency graph (18 published packages)
- Core API: NarrativeContext, SyncNarrativeContext, AsyncNarrativeContext, TracingLevel
- Data model: TraceTree, TraceNode, MethodSignature, ParameterCapture, TraceOutcome
- Proxy API: traceObject, ProxyOptions, decorators (@traced, @narrated, @onError, @notTraced)
- Concurrency: ForkJoinGroup (identity propagation, join wait-analysis), FireAndForgetGroup, ContextSnapshot (bidirectional propagation — async work joins the trace that launched it, reported from publication)
- Vitest API: narrativeTest, createNarrativeTest, createNarrativeTest(...).each, writeTraceOutput, writeStructuralOutput, evaluateApprovalTrace, ClaritySuiteReporter, StructuralSuiteReporter, ManifestSuiteReporter, runIdentity (the run has a name)
- Diagrams API: renderMermaidSequence, renderPlantUmlSequence
- Clarity API: analyzeClarity, renderClaritySuiteReport, exportClarityJson, the clarity gate CLI
- Runtime Adapters API: express, hono, nestjs, angular, react, react-router
- Observability API: observability enricher, opentelemetry bridge, winston, pino consumers
- Configuration: NarrativeTraceConfig, TracingLevel, RenderOptions, MarkdownOptions, NARRATIVETRACE_* env
- Architecture decisions: eager serialization, ALS vs stack-based context, frozen immutable data
- Troubleshooting: common issues and fixes
